answer.evidence: The tile is a flat, repeating stair pattern. Each step runs on an 8-row cycle: a light lip line (rows 0-1, 8, 16, 24), about 5-6 rows of textured stone tread, and 1-2 dark rows (rows 6-7, 14-15, 22-23, 30) that act as shadow or riser. Because the stairs descend away from the viewer, the treads are the visible horizontal surfaces and the risers face away. The only vertical face is the 1-2 dark rows per step, never 3 or more. There is no tall front face, so the tile reads as a top-down view of descending steps rather than a 3/4 block.
